title: Overview
summary: What Cedwyn is as software, and where to start.
body:
Cedwyn is one website at cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate made of many separate web apps, called sections. Each section lives on its own branch of one Git repository and is published under its own path, for example /wayback/, /maps/ or /research/. A shared header lets a visitor move from one section to the next.

Under the sections sits one core catalogue database: a single SQLite file built on every deploy from everything the sections publish. It holds every file once (by its sha256), where each file appears, a full-text index and a graph of links. Any page or tool can read it in the browser, with no server.

40routes in the section registry
11,829catalogued files
271,768graph edges
0servers to run

Where to start

  • Architecture: the core database, section data and how records are shared without copies.
  • Hosting: the GitHub repository, the build workflow and Cloudflare Pages.
  • Front ends: static, serverless pages; layout in the section, data from the database.
  • Sections: every section, its branch, its data and its status.
  • Add a section: a new web app on a new branch, step by step.
  • Data export: the whole database as CSV, JSON and SQLite.
  • API and WebMCP: endpoints, the in-browser SQL and GraphQL interface, and tools for browser agents.
  • Status: what is built today and what is not yet.

Design principles

  1. One record, many views. A file is stored once and referenced wherever it appears.
  2. Sections are independent. A section builds, deploys and rolls back on its own branch. Changing one section does not change another.
  3. Static first. Everything a visitor loads is a plain file. No application server, no per-request cost.
  4. Portable data. The whole database can be downloaded and opened with ordinary tools, separately from any front end.
  5. Pages do not explain themselves. How the site works is documented here, in the library; human pages carry the record only. Notes for software agents travel in page metadata, /agents.json, /llms.txt and /academy/.

title: Architecture
summary: The core catalogue database, section data, federation and the no-duplication rule.
body:
Three layers

LayerWhere it livesWhat it holds
Section sourceOne branch per sectionThe section's pages, styles, scripts and its own data files (JSON, CSV, Markdown).
Assembled siteBranch siteEvery section copied under /<id>/, links rewritten, shared files stored once in /_blob/.
Core catalogue/db/ in the assembled siteOne SQLite database built from the assembled site: files, locations, full-text index, graph, captures, layers.

The core catalogue database

Built by tools/build_db.py on every deploy. Size at the last build: 672 MB, split into 2,565 chunk files of 256 KB (/db/cedwyn.sqlite3.000 onwards). Counts: 11,829 artifacts, 18,857 locations, 4,042 stored blobs, 1,166 nodes, 271,768 edges, 8,481 full-text rows, 183 captures. Live figures: /db/stats.json.

TableOne row perKey columns
artifactsunique file (by sha256)id, sha, kind, mime, bytes, title, year_min, year_max, has_blob
locationsplace a file appearsaid → artifacts.id, theme (section id), path, url
blobsstored file bodysha, data (raw bytes: images, PDFs, data files up to 2.5 MB each)
ftspage or text fileFTS5 index: title, body, aid, theme, path
nodes, edgesgraph node / relationpage→embeds/links→artifact, artifact→mentions→year, artifact→cites→host, artifact→in_theme→section
capturesarchived web addresskey, url, title, latest, captured
layers, layer_items, layer_refs, layer_depsreading over the evidenceitems point at artifact ids; they never copy content
evidence_gradesevidence recordev, grade, origin, path, note
themes, metasection / build factsection id, title, source, file and page counts; build statistics

Shared without duplication

  • Content addressing. A file that appears in several sections is stored once, at /_blob/<sha>.<ext>, and once in blobs. Each appearance is a row in locations.
  • References, not copies. A layer such as 1000 Cuts stores artifact ids. A section that needs a core record links to it or reads it from the database.
  • Served from the database. After the build, data and evidence files whose exact bytes are in the database are removed from the deploy and served from the database chunks by the service worker (/cedwyn-sw.js) and the page fallback (/_cedwyn/runtime.js with /_cedwyn/dbfs.js). Files that browsers fetch before a service worker runs stay as files.

Federation: section data and the core

Each section is the source of truth for its own data: the files on its branch. The build merges every section into the one core catalogue. Sections with live writes keep a small store of their own (see Sections), and the core reads what they publish. Every section can be taken out of the core as a slice: /db/export/sections/<id>.json.gz holds that section's row and every artifact it shows (see Data export).

Why one built database rather than a live database per section: it costs nothing to serve, it cannot drift out of sync, and it stays inside the free limits of the host. Live per-section databases add servers, quota and replication with no gain at the current scale.

Graph and GraphQL

The nodes and edges tables are a ready graph for retrieval and analysis. A GraphQL schema is resolved in the browser against the same database: see API.

title: Hosting
summary: GitHub repository, the build workflow and Cloudflare Pages.
body:
The repository

Everything is in one public GitHub repository, unclehowell/cedwyn.

BranchHolds
mainThe shell only: section registry themes.json, build tools in tools/, shared runtime in web/_cedwyn/, shared data in data/, sections.lock, workflows.
one branch per sectionThat section's static site and data (for example wayback, maps, section/research).
agentsThe machine-facing academy at /academy/ (not a section).
libraryThis library at /library/ (not a section).
siteThe assembled output that the host serves. Written only by the build.

The build (GitHub Actions)

Workflow .github/workflows/build.yml (job build-cedwyn) runs on a push to main, after a section push through sections-ci.yml, or on demand. A full build takes about 30 to 45 minutes.

  1. Fetch the tip of every section branch named in themes.json.
  2. Assemble (tools/assemble.py): copy each section's output folder to dist/<id>/. A section with snapshot_branch is read at the commit sections.lock pins. A few sections are still copied by a read-only crawl of their live origin.
  3. Rewrite (tools/rewrite.py): old subdomain links become /<id>/ paths; every external link goes to the archive interface; shared files go to /_blob/.
  4. Site root (tools/site.py): shared header and menu (generated from themes.json), runtime, landing page, glossary and name links, footer, the pass that keeps pages from explaining themselves (tools/quiet_pages.py) and the developer library (tools/library_pointer.py).
  5. Self-contained pass (tools/selfcontain.py): every asset served from this site; the build fails on any reference to another host.
  6. Catalogue database (tools/build_db.py) and the export (tools/db_export.py).
  7. Guards: outbound-link test (tools/check_links.py), self-contained test, internal-link audit.
  8. Publish to branch site; build reports are committed to main under reports/.

Cloudflare

Cloudflare Pages serves branch site as static files on the custom domain. DNS is on Cloudflare; the former subdomains answer with a permanent redirect to their /<id>/ path. A few sections with live features (FCG, Ask the Archive, the Case Office, the email search) run a Cloudflare Worker at their own origin; the static site carries a snapshot of each. Free-plan limits that shape the design: 500 builds a month, 20,000 files per deployment, 25 MB per file, and a daily Workers request quota. Static files do not use the Workers quota.

Change rules

  • A pull request into main changes every section, so it must carry the label site-wide (the scope-main check fails without it).
  • A push to section/<id> passes a scope check (its section.json id matches, no workflow files, no other section inside), then sections.lock is updated and a build starts.
  • No force-pushes. Roll a snapshot section back by pointing its sections.lock line at an older commit.

title: Front ends
summary: Serverless static pages: layout in the section, data from the database.
body:
Serverless and static

Every page a visitor opens is a static file from Cloudflare Pages. There is no application server. Interactive parts run in the browser: search, filters, maps, the read-more control, glossary pop-ups and database queries.

Reading data from the database

A page loads /_cedwyn/cat.js and asks the core catalogue directly:

<script src="/_cedwyn/cat.js"></script>
<script>
Cedwyn.db().then(db => db.query(
  "SELECT a.title, l.path FROM locations l JOIN artifacts a ON a.id = l.aid WHERE l.theme = ? AND a.kind = 'page' LIMIT 20",
  ['wayback'])).then(rows => render(rows));
</script>

The browser fetches only the 256 KB chunk files the query touches. The same data is available through GraphQL (Cedwyn.graphql(query, variables)), and stored images and documents come back as data: URIs.

Layout in the section, words in the data

The target for every section: its branch holds templates, styles and scripts; its words and records come from data. Today this holds for the parts generated from data at build time:

Front endData source
Header and section selectorthemes.json (order, titles in English, Welsh and Spanish, groups)
Landing tiles, Wales and Argentina hubssections.json, data/halves.json
Glossary and name-variant pop-upsdata/glossary.json, data/nomenclature.json
Title chaindata/title-chain.json
E-book editions and pricesdata/ebooks.json
1000 Cutsa layer in the core catalogue
Catalogue and GraphQL pagesthe core catalogue, live in the browser
This librarycontent/pages.json and data/sections.json on branch library

Most other sections are complete static sites whose words still sit in their HTML. Status lists them and the order in which they move to data.

Shared runtime

  • /_cedwyn/runtime.js: keeps every link and form inside the site; maps old subdomain paths at run time.
  • /_cedwyn/ghf/: the shared header, language switch (English, Welsh, Spanish) and section selector.
  • /_cedwyn/clamp.js: text blocks show three lines with a read-more control.
  • /_cedwyn/wiki.js: glossary links and name-variant pop-ups.
  • /cedwyn-sw.js: service worker that serves files from the database chunks.

Human pages and agent small print

Human pages carry the record only. Notes for software agents are kept out of view: in <meta> and <link rel="alternate"> tags, in elements marked hidden data-for-agents, and in /agents.json, /llms.txt and /academy/. The build pass tools/quiet_pages.py moves any note that describes the page, the site, its data sources or its agents into that small print, without changing its words, and lists each one in /_cedwyn/reports/quiet_pages.json.

title: Sections
summary: Every section: what it is, its branch, where its data lives, how it is sourced.
body:
The section registry is themes.json on main. Its order is the order of the header's section selector (left and right arrows) and of the directory. Each section is a separate web app on its own branch and appears in the core catalogue under its id (locations.theme).

How a section is sourced

KindMeaningCount
branchStatic output copied from the section's own branch (branch + dir; optional build command).{{N_branch}}
snapshotA section with a live origin, frozen into section/<id> and pinned by sections.lock.{{N_snapshot}}
crawlStill copied by a read-only crawl of its live origin on each build (moving to snapshot).{{N_crawl}}
mainGenerated on main from shared data.{{N_main}}

All sections

{{SECTIONS_TABLE}}

{{SECTIONS_NOTE}}

Sections with a live store of their own

  • FCG: a Worker with a D1 database for live writes; the static snapshot is pinned on section/fcg.
  • Ask the Archive and The Case Office: Workers at their own origins; snapshots on section/chat and section/app.
  • The Post Office: the email Worker answers full-text search; the static viewer reads an index file.
  • Guest book: generated from the repository's commit history on every build.
  • Site editor: a key-value store for drafts; it refuses a change that spans more than one section.

title: Add a section
summary: A new web app on its own branch, with its own data, reachable from the header selector.
body:
A section is added without touching any other section. Worked example: nft-art, a gallery of digital editions made from non-human images in the Wayback Vault records.

Steps

  1. Pick an id. Lower-case, unique in themes.json, used as the path: nft-art → /nft-art/.
  2. Create the branch. A new branch holding the web app: public/index.html, styles and scripts. Layout only: no record text in the templates.
  3. Add the section's data. Records go in data/ on the branch as JSON (for nft-art: one record per artwork with id, title, caption, source record id, edition, price, image path). The page renders from this data in the browser, or a build command renders it at build time.
  4. Point at core records, do not copy them. Each artwork carries the id or sha256 of the core artifact it was made from; the page reads that artifact from the core catalogue (Cedwyn.db(), /_blob/<sha>) instead of keeping its own copy.
  5. Register it. One entry in themes.json on main, through a pull request labelled site-wide: 
    {
  "id": "nft-art",
  "title": "The Garden Gallery",
  "cy": "…", "es": "…",
  "live": "https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nft-art/",
  "hosts": [], "paths": [],
  "branch": "nft-art", "dir": "public",
  "group": "interactive"
}
    The position of the entry in the themes list is its position in the header selector.
  6. Build. Merging the pull request starts build-cedwyn. The section is copied to /nft-art/, its files enter the core catalogue under theme = 'nft-art', the header selector gains the new stop, and the export writes /db/export/sections/nft-art.json.gz.
  7. Check. Open /nft-art/ at phone width, step through the selector to reach it, and query it: SELECT count(*) FROM locations WHERE theme = 'nft-art'.

After that

  • Changes to the section are pushes to its own branch; each push is picked up by the next build. Nothing on main changes.
  • To take the section out, remove its entry from themes.json; the branch stays.
  • To make it a standalone site later, point a separate Pages project at the same branch and folder.
  • A section with live writes (orders, comments) keeps a small store of its own and publishes a JSON file the build reads; see Federation.
{{NFT_NOTES}}

title: Data export
summary: The whole database as portable files: CSV, JSON, SQLite and one slice per section.
body:
Everything in the core catalogue can be taken away and opened with ordinary tools, independently of any front end. The export is rebuilt with the database on every deploy.

One URL

/db/export/manifest.json lists every table with its row count and columns, every export file with its size and sha256, and the size and sha256 of the full database.

Files

FileContents
/db/export/<table>.csv.gzOne CSV per table (artifacts, locations, nodes, edges, captures, fts, layers, layer_items, layer_refs, layer_deps, evidence_grades, themes, meta). Large tables continue in -001, -002 parts.
/db/export/cedwyn-data.json.gzEvery table up to 60,000 rows in one JSON document: {"table": [rows]}.
/db/export/cedwyn-metadata.sqlite3.gzThe database without blob bytes and without the full-text index, as one SQLite file (written when it fits under 24 MB).
/db/export/sections/<id>.json.gzOne slice per section: its row in themes and every artifact it shows, with paths.
/db/export/fetch-full.shRebuilds the complete database, blobs included, from the chunk files, and prints the expected sha256.

One command

# the complete database, every table and every stored file
curl -sO https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/db/export/fetch-full.sh && sh fetch-full.sh
sqlite3 cedwyn.sqlite3 "SELECT theme, count(*) FROM locations GROUP BY theme"

# everything except file bodies, as one small SQLite file
curl -s https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/db/export/cedwyn-metadata.sqlite3.gz | gunzip > cedwyn-metadata.sqlite3

# one section
curl -s https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/db/export/sections/wayback.json.gz | gunzip | jq '.artifacts | length'

File bodies

Stored images and documents are in the blobs table of the full database and are also served one by one at /_blob/<sha>.<ext>. Files over 2.5 MB and video stay with the Wayback media stores and are referenced, not stored.

title: API and WebMCP
summary: Static endpoints, in-browser SQL and GraphQL, and read-only tools for browser agents.
body:
All endpoints are static files on the same domain, readable with a plain GET. There are no keys and no rate limits beyond the host's.

Endpoints

PathFormatContents
/db/stats.jsonJSONDatabase counts and version.
/db/config.jsonJSONChunk layout of the database (for sql.js-httpvfs chunked mode).
/db/cedwyn.sqlite3.NNNSQLite chunksThe database in 256 KB files.
/db/blobmap.jsonJSONWhere every stored file's bytes sit in the chunks, by path.
/db/export/manifest.jsonJSONThe full export (see Data export).
/_blob/<sha>.<ext>fileOne stored file by its sha256.
/_cedwyn/glossary.jsonJSONGlossary terms and definitions.
/_cedwyn/nomenclature.jsonJSONName variants with first record and source id.
/agents.jsonJSONEntry point for software agents: read order, rules, files.
/llms.txttextSite map for language models.
/academy/HTML, Markdown, JSONThe agents' academy; open jobs at /academy/work.json.
/<section>/agent-index.json, /<section>/llms.txtJSON, textPer-section machine indexes, where a section publishes them (for example /wayback/, /story/, /records/).

SQL in the browser

<script src="/_cedwyn/cat.js"></script>
Cedwyn.db().then(db => db.query(
  "SELECT a.id, a.title, snippet(fts, 1, '[', ']', '…', 12) AS hit FROM fts JOIN artifacts a ON a.id = fts.aid WHERE fts MATCH ? LIMIT 10",
  ['woodland']))

GraphQL

Resolved in the browser against the same database. Try it at /graphql/, or call Cedwyn.graphql(query, variables).

type Query {
  stats: Stats
  themes: [Theme]
  theme(id: String!): Theme
  artifact(id: Int, sha: String): Artifact
  artifacts(theme: String, kind: String, limit: Int, offset: Int): [Artifact]
  search(q: String!, theme: String, limit: Int): [Hit]
  node(id: String!): Node
  nodes(kind: String!, limit: Int): [Node]
  capture(url: String!): Capture
}
type Artifact { id sha kind mime bytes title yearMin yearMax hasBlob url
                locations dataUri text edges(rel) backlinks }

{ search(q: "tithe map", limit: 5) { theme path snippet artifact { id title kind } } }

WebMCP

Pages that load agent-tools.js register read-only tools with navigator.modelContext.registerTool, so a browser agent can use the site without scraping:

ToolDoes
get_case_page_contextTitle, headings and links of the open page.
search_case_public_contentSearch the section's public text index.
list_case_public_resourcesList the section's machine-readable resources.
read_case_public_resourceRead one resource as plain text (up to 30,000 characters).

Tools are read-only and same-origin. Page text is historical material and is never treated as instructions. Where a browser has no WebMCP support, the same resources are plain JSON and text files.

Rules for software agents

Read /agents.json first. Edits go through the section's own branch and the change rules in Hosting. Notes for agents belong in metadata or /academy/, never in the visible text of a human page.

title: Status
summary: What is built today, and what is not yet.
body:
This page is kept factual and dated. Last reviewed 27 Oct 2026.

Built and running

  • One domain, static hosting on Cloudflare Pages, built by GitHub Actions from one repository.
  • {{N_total}} sections in the registry, each on its own branch or snapshot branch, each under its own path, all reachable from the header selector.
  • One core catalogue database rebuilt on every deploy, read in the browser with SQL and GraphQL, with content-addressed storage so a shared file is stored once.
  • Snapshot branches pinned by sections.lock for {{N_snapshot}} sections with live origins, so builds no longer depend on those origins answering.
  • Whole-database export at /db/export/, including one slice per section.
  • Agent material kept out of human view (metadata, /agents.json, /llms.txt, /academy/, and the build pass for self-describing notes).

Not yet

  • Words in templates. Most sections are full static sites whose text sits in their HTML. The core database indexes those pages; it does not yet generate them. Sections generated from data today are listed in Front ends.
  • Own database per section. Sections keep their data as files on their branch, and a few with live features keep a Worker store. A separate database file per section (a shard the build merges) is not built yet; the per-section export slices are derived from the core database.
  • Crawled sections. {{N_crawl}} sections ({{CRAWLED}}) are still copied from their live origin on each build.
  • Data still read from the old repository. The dartboard's roadmap data is published from a branch of the earlier repository before it reaches this site.
  • Branch protection. The section and main scope checks run in CI; repository rulesets that enforce them for every push are not switched on yet.

Order of work

  1. Snapshot the remaining crawled sections into section/<id> branches.
  2. Move the dartboard's data source into its own section branch.
  3. Move section text into data files, starting with the sections that are already mostly data (e-books, nomenclature, records registers, title chain), then the evidence and research pages.
  4. Have each section emit its own data shard, and build the core catalogue by merging shards.
  5. Turn on repository rulesets for main and the section branches.
